name: schema_service.py
summary: Service class that manages dataset schema inference, validation, and serialization operations within the dataset domain.
purpose: Encapsulates schema-related business logic to decouple data structure analysis from dataset lifecycle management, providing a centralized domain service for consistent schema handling across the application.
responsibilities: Inferring column types, structures, and metadata from dataset contents using pandas
Validating dataset schemas against structural constraints and business rules
Serializing and deserializing schema definitions using JSON
Managing filesystem interactions and environment-specific paths via os and Django settings
Supporting downstream dataset operations with schema-aware logic
inputs: Raw dataset files, DataFrames, or tabular data streams
Schema configuration parameters and validation rules
Filesystem paths and Django settings references
outputs: Validation results, error reports, or conformance flags
Serialized schema artifacts and inferred type mappings
architecture_notes: Implements the Service Layer pattern within a Django app architecture, isolating schema-specific domain logic from views, models, and data access layers. Positioned as a dedicated collaborator to the main DatasetService, following the Single Responsibility Principle. Leverages pandas for data profiling, json for schema serialization, and Django settings for environment-specific configuration, placing it in the domain services tier of the backend.
improvements: Introduce explicit type hints and schema dataclasses to clarify service contracts and improve IDE support
Abstract pandas and filesystem dependencies behind adapter or repository interfaces to reduce coupling and enhance unit testability
Add structured custom exceptions for schema validation failures instead of propagating low-level library errors
Implement caching for repeated schema inference operations to reduce computational overhead on identical datasets
Consider adding schema versioning and evolution tracking if managing long-lived or frequently updated dataset structures
